text:
If it's still clear and calm out your window right now, don't get too comfortable, that's about to change. We're sitting at 81 with a light south wind, but the forecasters have this flipping fast, with showers and thunderstorms firing up between 1 and 4 this afternoon and sticking around into the evening. The high near 85 is believable, though the Euro wants closer to 88 and is far wetter than the American model, so I'd lean toward the soggier outcome. Storms could pack a punch locally, a tenth to a quarter inch, and untangling the exact timing today isn't easy.

Tonight the rain gets more persistent, half an inch or more possible, and forecasters are flagging isolated flash flooding if storms train over the same spots, mainly overnight into Wednesday. The lake's manageable through this afternoon, waves 1 to 3 feet, but I'd be off the water well before the evening storms arrive and stay off through Wednesday's steadier, cooler rain in the mid 70s.

WCAX METEOROLOGIST: Tuesday night and through Wednesday brings more steady rain shower activity that could be heavier at times, especially across southern Vermont. Rain amounts will be highly variable depending on where the heaviest downpours set up Tuesday and Wednesday. In general, the farther south you are, the more likely you are to see excessive rain. The farther north you are, the less likely you are to see a lot of rain. Totals will likely be enhanced in the central and southern Green Mountains, Adirondacks and communities on the southeastern slopes. The Upper Valley and I-91 corridor in southern Vermont could also see higher amounts.
